takeaways.label: Strong quarter, guidance held
takeaways.text: Consolidated revenue grew 23% YoY with US up 42%, and full-year constant-currency growth guidance was maintained at 15%.

takeaways.label: CDMO is the growth engine
takeaways.text: CDMO revenue grew 31% YoY, driven by commercial supply of signed contracts and new manufacturing partnerships, and the pipeline quality is described as better than ever.

takeaways.label: Cenexi loss was planned, recovery promised
takeaways.text: The EUR 6 million EBITDA loss was driven by a planned summer shutdown; management expects profitability to return from Q3 and full-year guidance of EUR 20 million at high single-digit margin remains on track.

takeaways.label: Capacity is now the binding constraint
takeaways.text: Liquid vial utilization hit 92% and is heading to ~102%, forcing deferral of planned shutdowns and triggering a ₹1,000 crore brownfield expansion plus a new greenfield project.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether Cenexi profitability actually returns, the Saudi NUPCO tender outcome, and the capex quantum for the Vizag greenfield project.

points.label: CDMO as strategic anchor
points.text: The segment is growing faster than the base business and is described as the most important driver of long-term strategy, with commercial supply from previously signed contracts now converting into revenue.

points.label: Pipeline quality improving
points.text: Management stated the CDMO opportunity pipeline is robust, with both quality and scale of opportunities better than ever, providing increasing visibility and confidence in the future growth trajectory.

points.label: Microsphere contracts signed
points.text: Three royalty-based microsphere projects were secured during the quarter; one exhibit batch is complete and two more are in line, with revenue expected post 2029-2030.

points.label: Respiratory manufacturing win
points.text: A manufacturing contract for respiratory products was also secured during the quarter, adding to the CDMO portfolio breadth.

points.label: GLP-1 progress
points.text: One more GLP-1 project was signed recently with exhibit batches ongoing; some launches may occur in Q1 or Q2 of FY28, with milestone income and tech transfer fees booked in FY27.

points.label: In-licensing pipeline active
points.text: A second long-acting injectable product was in-licensed from China in the past two quarters, a $2 billion product still under patent with a ~3-year commercial timeline; clinicals will be done by Gland and manufacturing will remain in China.

quotes.text: Srinivas Sadu: "The CDMO business continues to emerge as a key growth engine for Gland Pharma and remains one of the most important drivers of our long-term strategy."

points.label: US revenue surged 42% YoY
points.text: Growth was driven by contribution from recent launches, increasing volumes from existing products, and continued momentum in CDMO programs.

points.label: Europe grew 23% YoY
points.text: Supported by increasing customer engagement, higher volumes from existing products, recent launches, and improving commercial traction across both CDMO and critical injectable business.

points.label: Four US launches in the quarter
points.text: The company launched four products in the US market and filed 11 ANDAs while receiving 10 approvals, sustaining a healthy launch cadence.

points.label: Methylprednisolone suspension approval
points.text: Received approval for a generic of Pfizer's Medrol, described as a large product, adding to the US portfolio.

points.label: New launches contribution
points.text: New launches are expected to contribute approximately 6-7% of growth going forward, providing a recurring tailwind.

points.label: ROW softness expected to reverse
points.text: Rest of world revenue was impacted by market-specific supply and tender-related dynamics, especially the delay of NUPCO tender results from Saudi Arabia; management expects ROW to improve in H2.

points.label: Saudi tender participation
points.text: 13 products were submitted for the NUPCO tender; management is confident on several products and expects the tender to open this quarter.

points.label: Q2 loss was planned
points.text: The EUR 6 million EBITDA loss and lower revenue at Cenexi were primarily due to planned annual summer shutdown activities; the underlying operating trend remains encouraging.

points.label: Full-year guidance intact
points.text: Management confirmed the previous guidance of EUR 20 crore EBITDA at high single-digit margin for FY2027 remains on track, with profitability expected to return from Q3 onwards.

points.label: Strategy prioritizes profit over growth
points.text: Cenexi's focus is on making operations more efficient and profitable rather than top-line growth; minimum revenue growth is expected while the rest of the business grows faster.

points.label: Cost reduction plan
points.text: The plan involves reducing headcount and investing in faster lines for operational efficiencies, though the transition will involve some shutdown periods as new lines are installed.

points.label: Investments on track
points.text: Planned investments including a new vial and lyophilization block at BLA and a high-speed ampoule line at Fontenay remain on track, expected to strengthen the platform's competitiveness.

points.label: Tax rate normalization expected
points.text: The elevated effective tax rate of ~33% in Q2 was largely attributable to Cenexi losses during the shutdown, since those losses are not eligible for tax benefits; normalization is expected as Cenexi returns to profitability from Q3.

quotes.text: Srinivas Sadu: "Cenexi, like earlier said, the growth, the focus is on making it more efficient and make profitable rather than the top line. There will be minimum growth from revenue perspective, but the idea is to make it more profitable."

points.label: Capacity constraints are acute
points.text: Liquid vial utilization is at 92% and expected to hit approximately 102% next year; ophthalmic, bags, and liquid vials are all struggling for capacity, and planned shutdowns on some lines are being deferred because no spare capacity exists to absorb the downtime.

points.label: Brownfield expansion at Pashamylaram
points.text: Board approved a ₹1,000 crore brownfield block with three isolator-based vial manufacturing lines; commercial operations are anticipated to commence from FY2030, with a two-year completion timeline to meet demand from signed contracts.

points.label: Greenfield project at Vizag SEZ
points.text: Land has been acquired and project planning is underway; full capex quantum will be presented for Board approval next quarter, with a four-year phased build program.

points.label: Bag line awaiting FDA inspection
points.text: Additional bag manufacturing capacity has been installed during the year and is awaiting US FDA inspection; commercialization post-inspection will de-bottleneck capacity constraints for product supplies.

points.label: Capex philosophy
points.text: The ₹3,000 crore investment program is backed by contracts in place or at minimum forecasts; the greenfield project is driven by the broader business environment and capacity running out, and will be built in phases.

quotes.text: Srinivas Sadu: "We actually, we're supposed to take shutdowns a couple of lines, but we're not taking because we don't have capacity to fill if we take shutdown. So that's the situation we are in."

points.label: EBITDA margin improved to 26%
points.text: Up from approximately 21% YoY, supported by stronger revenue, increasing CDMO contribution, favorable business mix, operating leverage, and ongoing efficiency initiatives, despite significantly higher R&D investment.

points.label: Gross margin stable YoY at 63%
points.text: Productivity improvements, manufacturing optimization, alternate sourcing, and yield enhancement initiatives offset headwinds; the sequential decline from 65% to 63.5% was driven by Cenexi's lower revenue during the shutdown, since Cenexi carries higher gross margins.

points.label: R&D spend stepped up
points.text: Expenditure increased to ₹107.7 crore (6% of revenue) from ₹77.2 crore in the previous quarter, focused on complex injectables including suspensions, peptides, hormones, and ophthalmic solutions; a slight increase is expected over time due to product complexity, but margin levels will be maintained.

points.label: Working capital improved
points.text: Working capital days improved to 158 days driven primarily by inventory optimization initiatives and enhanced inventory management practices.

points.label: Other income declined sequentially
points.text: The reduction versus Q1 FY27 was largely due to a change in FX gain/loss.

points.label: Two successful FDA inspections
points.text: The Vizag oncology facility completed a US FDA inspection with zero observations; the Dundigal facility underwent inspection in October and concluded with four procedural observations, with neither data integrity observations nor repeat observations.

points.label: New CEO joining
points.text: Mr. Deepak Sapra will join as CEO on November 16th, filling a key leadership position.

points.label: Cenexi President onboarded
points.text: Mr. Ajay Sahni joined earlier in the week of the call as President of Cenexi operations, strengthening local leadership for the turnaround.

points.label: Senior hires across functions
points.text: New heads of tech transfer, strategy and innovative medicines (India), and business development (China) were onboarded, along with two senior project management hires; a Chief Investment Officer based in China will also join, with a global role covering acquisitions including US biologics and in-licensing complex products from China.

points.label: US biologics acquisition approach
points.text: Management will not pursue loss-making or very low EBITDA assets, preferring profitable assets even at a higher price; focus is on contracts commercializing in year two and quality of the management team, with a stated preference for US over European plants.

points.label: India market entry via innovation
points.text: The company plans to enter the Indian market with innovative in-licensed products rather than generics, leveraging Fosun subsidiaries and other partners, with lower investment required for India-only rights.

quotes.text: Srinivas Sadu: "One thing is probably not be looking at a loss-making or a very low EBITDA asset. Even if you have to pay a little higher, but we will go with a profitable asset."

items.title: Group 20% growth guide
items.text: With the new MSA contract and other deals under discussion, management raised its growth outlook to ~20% annually over the next 4 years, up from the earlier 15% CAGR, with near-term consolidated EBITDA target of 30%. That compounds the current ₹7,072 cr revenue base to roughly double in four years, with CDMO margins 5-10% better than the core business.

items.title: Global CDMO MSA - 55 SKUs
items.text: A Manufacturing and Supply Agreement signed 9 Aug 2026 with a leading global pharma company covers 55 sterile injectable SKUs across 3 Indian sites, with tech transfer starting September 2026 and revenue from CY2029, annualizing at USD 90-100 million. That is ~12% of current revenue at full ramp, enabled by the Cenexi acquisition, with a ₹165 cr oncology isolator line already being installed by January 2027.

items.title: ₹5,000 cr capacity build-out
items.text: Gland is executing ~₹5,000 cr of capex over 4 years - ₹2,000 cr base brownfield, ₹1,000 cr for 3 isolator vial lines at Pashamylaram (commercial from FY30), plus a Vizag greenfield - adding ~300-400 crore units to current ~170 crore unit capacity. The trigger is real: liquid vial lines run at 92% utilization, lyo at 80-90%, and ophthalmic and bag capacity already cannot meet demand.

items.title: GLP-1 fill-and-finish
items.text: Eight GLP-1 contracts are signed (Liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide) with 6-7 more expected, cartridge capacity is tripling from 4 to 14 crore units, and Gland is in talks with a major insulin player for the line's capacity. US liraglutide launched in January, FY27 brings milestone and tech-transfer income, and material US volumes arrive FY30-31 as patents expire.

items.title: US launch cadence
items.text: Sugammadex (US market ~USD 1.6 bn) launched Day 1 after 29 Jul 2026 approval, Methylprednisolone (USD 214 mn market) was approved 3 Nov 2026, and MVI launched with CGT exclusivity, on top of 31 US launches in FY26 and GPO contract wins that lifted quarterly run-rate to ~USD 110 million. US revenue grew 42% YoY in Q2 FY27 to ₹1,179.5 cr, and management says the growth is not one-off.

items.title: Cenexi turnaround to €200 mn
items.text: Cenexi turned EBITDA-positive in Q4 FY26 and management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of €200 mn revenue at high single-digit margin, implying H2 at 18-20% margin, with a mid-term goal of mid-teen EBITDA. New Fontenay and Braine lines, a hormonal prefilled-syringe contract and 3 Gland product launches via Cenexi from Q3 FY27 add to the recovery.

items.title: Complex CDMO contract stack
items.text: A European CMS project (USD 2.5-3 crore annual potential) commercializes H2 FY28, a new oncology contract adds USD 25-30 mn from FY28, three royalty-based microsphere projects were signed in Q2 FY27, and FY26 signings add USD 4-5 crore of CDMO revenue in FY27. Milestone and profit-share income already ran ~₹297 cr in Q2 FY27, about 16% of revenue.

items.title: RTU bags and complex pipeline
items.text: 24 ready-to-use bag products are filed with 18 approved, addressing a ~USD 640 mn US market, while 15 co-development products (505(b)(2) and ANDAs) target commercialization from FY29. Management flags a step-up to ~19-20% growth in FY29 as a couple of large microsphere complex products launch in Q2/Q3 FY29.

items.title: China in-licensing and Novelstar
items.text: A Q2 FY27 term sheet adds a second long-acting injectable from China (a USD 2 bn under-patent product), following an USD 800 mn product to be made in India, plus a liposomal product with US/EU rights timed to patent expiry. The USD 21 mn Novelstar investment, completing by 31 Oct 2026, supports US expansion through a strategic partnership with promoter-group Fosun Pharma USA.
